entries.acceptance: Select ordinary-hit, head-hit, weapon-miss or unarmed-miss outcomes from the actual action and target. Head outcomes apply to face, skull and eye. Unarmed outcomes include natural attacks, grappling, collisions and unarmed parries by creatures. Reconcile detailed combat exceptions before dispatch.
Critical multipliers modify basic damage before armor and injury factors. Critical hits disallow active defense. Preserve separate damage, penetration and injury values.

entries.acceptance: Rolls 3-4 critically succeed; 5 requires effective skill at least 15 and 6 requires at least 16. Check detailed combat eligibility and exceptions rather than globally changing ordinary checks.

Roll 18 critically fails. Roll 17 critically fails at effective skill 15 or below, otherwise ordinarily fails. Failure margin at least ten critically fails melee attacks and defenses; B382 explicitly excludes ranged attacks despite the generic B556 summary. Apply firearm malfunction priority before table dispatch.

entries.acceptance: Solid crushing weapons, enchanted weapons, fine/very-fine weapons and most firearms require another critical-miss table roll before breaking. Wheel-lock, guided-missile and beam categories are exceptions to firearm resistance. A second breakage result breaks the weapon; any other result drops it. Preserve quality, construction and attack-category inputs.
entries.validation_note: Supplied-roll assessment and owned drop branches authored; fixtures unrun. Actual breakage, flinging, weapon-specific overrides and automatic combat dispatch remain incomplete.

entries.acceptance: For impaling/piercing melee and every ranged attack, a self-hit result requires a second table roll. Another self-hit uses the second result’s full/half damage; any other result replaces the original. Do not recursively repeat this exception.

A combatant unable to fall, including one already down, substitutes 1d-3 general injury for unarmed fall results. A flying/swimming combatant instead enters an awkward position with attack -4 and defense -3; specify restoration through movement/posture rules. Preserve injury rounding rules rather than allowing healing from negative dice.

Commit critical outcomes through shared injury, equipment, condition and tactical state. Retain precise expiry, body part and source identity across undo/save, and avoid rolling a second table during preview or applying a consequence twice.
